FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Fasteners for Consumer Goods and Hair Cutting, Shaving, Shearing and Allied 
Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical Engineering 
Division Council. 

This standard would help the manufacturers for selecting the right material for the manufacturing 
of the cashes used to keep the barbers tools. This standard also provides the necessary guidance to 
the barbers for selecting the right product. Since this product is being used extensively by military 
and paramilitary forces, the assistance has been derived from the Joint-Service Specification 
JSS 7105-18 while preparing this standard. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded oJBFin accordance with IS 2 : 1960 *Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised y* 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard. 



IS 14232 : 1995 



Indian Standard 

SHAVING SYSTEMS — CASES FOR BARBERS 
TOOLS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This specification covers the requirements 
of cases for barbers tools. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this Standard: 



Title

leather ( second revision ) 

Specification for non-ferrous 
rivets ( 1-6 to 10 mm ) 

Specification for buckles {first 
revision )

sewing threads

3 MATERIAL 

3.1 The cases for barbers tools shall be 
manufactured from the appropriate materials 
specified in the relevant specifications given 
below: 



Material! Specification 

— Leather, cow/bufiFalo, cur- 
ried conforming to IS 580 : 
1973 

— Buckle brass roller single, 
16 mm and 25 mm sizes 
conforming to IS 4274 : 
1981 

— Flax-undyed conforming to 
IS 9543 : 1980 

— Rivets copper hose, 
tinned 3 mm with washer 
conforming to IS 2907 : 
1964 

Wax shoe maker — The material shall have the 
and saddlers following properties

water boil for 5 
minutes ) . 

4 MANUFACTURE 

4.1 The cases for barbers tools shall be 
manufactured to the shape and design as shown 
in Fig. 1 and 2. 

4.2 The metallic fasteners shall be firmly 
attached to the leather in required positions so 
that each fastener shall fit into the correspond- 
ing leather strap without producing any 
tension or sagging in the strap. 

4.3 The stitching shall be uniform, sound, neat 
and shall be regulated at 28 to 30 stitches per 
decimeter. The thread shall be of 4 cord well 
twisted and waxed. Sewing by hook awl method 
shall not be permitted. 

5 DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES 

5.1 The case shall conform to the dimensions 
given in Fig. 1 and 2. 

5.2 Tolerances on dimensions shall be as shown 
in Fig. 1 and 2 and tolerance on thickness shall 
be as per IS 580 : 1973. 

6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

6.1 The metallic fittings shall be properly made 
to shape and shall be free from cracks, seams, 
scales, burrs and other defects. The buckle 
shall be finished smooth and the rollers shall be 
in a condition to move freely over the arms of 
the buckles. 

6.2 All leather shall be cleanly cut and edges 
shall be neatly rubbed and creased. 

6.3 All stitchings shall be of even tension and 
securely fastened off. The loose ends of the 
threads shall be removed. 

6.4 The general workmanship and finish shall 
be good or as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the manufacturer.

7 MARKING 

7.1 Each case shall be legibly and indelibly 
marked with the manufacturer's name or 
recognised trade-mark, number and year of 
manufacture. 

7.2 BIS Certification Marking 

The product may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 

7.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed 
by the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made 
thereunder. The details of conditions under 
which the licence for the use of Standard Mark 
may be granted to manufacturers or producers 
may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian 
Standards. 

8 PACKING 

8.1 Each case shall be suitably packed in 
accordance with the acceptable trade practice 
or as agreed to between the purchaser and 
the manufacturer. 

9 SAMPLING 

9.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer the sampling 
plan as given in Tables 1 and 2 shall be 
followed. 



9,2 The samples shall be drawn using the 
technique of random sampling as per IS 4905 : 
1968.

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to 
promote harmoious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Gopyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced 
in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, 
in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type 
or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director 
( Publications ), BIS. 

ReTision of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards 
are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review 
indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken 
up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the 
latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 'BIS Handbook' and 'Standards 
Monthly Addition',
